The Committee on Anti-dumping oversees the implementation of the Agreement on Anti-dumping and provides a forum for members to raise and address related questions and concerns. The current chair is
Informal Group on Anti-Circumvention
In a Decision on Anti-Circumvention at Marrakesh, Ministers noted that while the problem of circumvention of anti-dumping measures formed part of the Uruguay Round negotiations on anti-dumping, negotiators were unable to agree on specific text, and decided to refer this matter to the Committee on Anti-Dumping Practices for resolution. Pursuant to this Ministerial Decision, Members established the Informal Working Group on Anti-Circumvention at a meeting of the Anti-Dumping Committee held in September 1997. (See minutes in
Working Group on Implementation
The Working Group on Implementation was created by decision of the Committee on Ant-Dumping Practices in October 1996
.  The Working Group serves as a forum for the exchange of information on Member practices.
The  data presented in the tables below are taken from the semi-annual reports of  WTO Members to the Committee on Anti-Dumping Practices and cover the period 1  January 1995 – 31 December 2025. The tables are based on information from Members  having submitted semi-annual reports for the relevant periods, and are  incomplete to the extent Members have not submitted reports, or have submitted  incomplete reports. For the purpose of these tables, each initiation and  measure reported covers one product imported from one country.  "Country" in each case refers to country or customs territory  (referred to in the tables as "Exporter"). The information in the  tables will be updated periodically.
